comment: Single source of truth for performance scenes (Rust vs Bullet wall-clock comparison; docs/bullet-perf.md). tools/generate_perf_scenes.py expands the parameterized generators into static body tables: tools/bullet_perf_scenes.h (C++ runner, tools/bullet_perf.cpp) and crates/bullet/src/perf_scenes_table.rs (Rust runner, crates/bullet/examples/perf_scenes.rs); do not edit the generated files. Unlike tools/scenes.json (parity), bodies come from deterministic generators (never listed by hand): 'box_grid' stacks nx*ny*nz boxes, 'mixed_rain' drops a deterministic box/sphere/capsule lattice, 'chains' builds a grid of fixed-base multibody pendulums, 'mesh_rain' drops dynamic triangle-mesh shells (GImpact). dt is [num, den]; warmup frames run before timing; iterations is the PGS count. broadphase_aabb is the sweep-extent hint for btAxisSweep3 (our AxisSweep3 is unbounded; the hint only scopes the C++ side).

stack_1000.comment: Solver stress: a 10x10x10 box stack settling on a box ground. 600 frames cover the active settle (~2s) plus the sleeping steady state; last300_ms reports the steady-state window.

rain_500.comment: Narrow phase + broad phase stress: 500 mixed convex bodies (box/sphere/capsule lattice, 10x10 grid x 5 layers) raining onto a wavy 20x20 height mesh (deterministic amp*sin(ax*x)*cos(az*z) heights).

mb_chains.comment: Featherstone ABA + multibody constraint stress: a 20x10 grid (200) of fixed-base 3-link revolute pendulums released from 60 degrees. Link colliders are 0.1 spheres in the DefaultFilter group (required for the C++ island solver); the chains never touch each other, so this isolates the articulated dynamics path at a realistic scale (the original 5x4/20-chain grid ran ~45us/frame, too small to separate engine cost from launch noise).

dbvt_rain_2000.comment: Large-scale dynamic scene for the Dbvt broad phase: 2000 mixed convex bodies (20x20 grid x 5 layers) raining onto a wavy 40x40 height mesh. Both sides run their dynamic-BVH broad phase (Bullet's default btDbvtBroadphase vs this crate's DbvtBroadPhase via BroadPhaseBackend::Dbvt) - the sweep scenes above compare the other algorithm.

gimpact_rain_100.comment: Dynamic concave mesh (GImpact) stress: 100 closed triangle-mesh shells (12-triangle boxes) rain onto a wavy 40x40 height mesh. Every shell-vs-terrain and shell-vs-shell pair runs the mesh-mesh path (tree-vs-tree candidate query + per-triangle-pair GJK with the margin shell), matching Bullet's btGImpactMeshShape via the registered GImpact collision algorithm. The drop is deliberately low (touchdown ~4.5 m/s, one-step travel < the 0.1 margin band) - zero-thickness panels can tunnel when a single step exceeds the band (docs/bullet-deviations.md). A stacking variant was tried and rejected: both engines collapse gimpact stacks (Bullet worse - its shells end up tunneled through the ground), so the two sides' workloads diverge and the numbers are meaningless; see docs/bullet-deviations.md.

cloth_wind.comment: Soft-body core stress (links + faces PBD + aerodynamics): a 4x4 grid of 16 pinned cloths (12x12 nodes each, ~2700 nodes / ~4600 triangles total) under a constant wind with the V_TwoSided aero model. The cloths are pinned at all four corners and hang in the air (no ground below), so the wind keeps every node active the whole run - a steady-state full-rate soft-body load with zero contact work. Per-cloth corners are laid out on a deterministic grid (origin + col/row * (size + gap)); the 'softs' spec is passed to both runners and expanded by CreatePatch/create_patch (the byte-exact helpers already probe-verified in the softbody phases).

softbody_rain.comment: Soft-body contact stress (SDF_RS node-vs-rigid at scale): 64 free cloths (8x8 grid of 6x6 patches, ~3100 nodes total) settle onto a static ground plane from a low drop (y=0.5, ~2.2 m/s - a faster drop tunnels Bullet's own cloths through the plane, the rope_ball_tunnel catch-leak class, and the two workloads diverge). After touchdown every cloth node sits in the contact band and the classic per-node SDF_RS route runs at full rate for the rest of the run (soft bodies never sleep). Nodes are laid out identically to cloth_wind (deterministic grid, CreatePatch/create_patch).

softbody_mesh.comment: Soft-body contact stress on a triangulated terrain (the SDF cache's home turf): the softbody_rain workload with the analytic ground plane swapped for the same wavy 40x40 static mesh the other scenes use (~3200 triangles). Bullet's soft-vs-concave route pays its sparse-SDF voxel pipeline here by design (this is the workload the 0.25 m voxel cache was built for), while our node-vs-triangle distance walks the local BVH every query - so this scene decomposes the softbody_rain lead into the SDF-pipeline share (visible as the gap against softbody_rain's plane number) and the shared implementation share. Same 64 cloths, same drop (y = 0.5; the terrain peaks at y = 0.2 so the first touch is ~2.4 m/s), never sleeps.

game_arena.comment: Game-realistic load profile: the point is not body count (the rain/stack scenes already cover 500-2000 bodies) but sustained activity - a launcher throws a ball into the box tower every 0.5 s (20 balls over the run) while a heavy driven ball (mass 50, body #1, velocity-scripted along x = 4*sin(2*pi*t/240)) plows back and forth through the props. Typical games keep ~100-300 active bodies; this runs ~67 initial props (48-box tower + 25 scattered boxes + 9 shells + 9 mixed props) growing to ~88 with the stream, so contacts stay hot the whole run instead of settling like a one-shot rain. The 'script' field selects the deterministic per-frame arena tick both runners implement (launcher + dozer velocity); bodies[1] must stay the dozer (mass 50 sphere).
